claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with an as-cast fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a strength of approximately 944 MPa.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has approximately 25% tensile ductility.
Cold working AlCoCrFeNi2.1 beyond roughly 10–20% strain increases strength at the expense of ductility.
Cold-worked AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can exceed approximately 1200 MPa strength while its ductility falls to approximately 10%.
Applying 10–20% cold deformation followed by a 700–800°C, approximately one-hour heat treatment and rapid quenching will refine the fcc/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The proposed processing will reduce the interlamellar spacing.
The proposed processing will produce more coherent interfaces between the fcc and B2 regions.
The heat treatment will cause partial recovery and recrystallization at phase interfaces after mild cold work.
A refined, coherent lamellar architecture can facilitate dislocation slip across phase interfaces.
Dislocation shearing across coherent lamellae can alleviate local stress concentrations rather than nucleating cracks.
The refined fcc/B2 interfaces will promote more effective strain hardening.
The proposed treatment will simultaneously increase strength and ductility in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The treated alloy will have significantly greater strength than the as-cast alloy.
The treated alloy will maintain or improve ductility relative to cold work alone.
The proposed benefit is restricted to approximately 10–20% deformation and a 700–800°C heat treatment lasting about one hour.
Excessive deformation or deviations from the stated thermal window may cause grain coarsening or undesirable phase transformations.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy retains excellent mechanical properties up to 700°C.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis asserts increased strength and ductility, but the predicted outcome only requires ductility to be maintained or improved relative to the ductility-degraded cold-worked state. The falsification rule alternates between requiring an increase in both properties and merely requiring ductility not to fall below the as-cast value.
